Question 10 of 11 · The Quran

The Quran's literary challenge

The Quran challenged its audience to produce a single chapter like it. What exactly is that challenge?

The case

The Quran challenged all of Arabia — masters of the Arabic language — to produce even one chapter like it. 1400 years later, no one has.

This challenge, called the 'Tahaddi', is still open.

Why this is significant

7th-century Arabs were masters of poetry and rhetoric. The Quran was revealed in their own language, and they were unable to match it despite every motivation to do so.

Read more

Arab linguists who opposed Islam admitted they had never heard anything like the Quran. It defied all known categories of Arabic speech.

Objections, answered

The strongest pushback we hear, and our answer to each.

You might say“Literary quality is subjective”

Our answer

The challenge is more specific than style.

More than beauty

The challenge combines linguistic precision, internal consistency, depth of meaning, and predictive accuracy. The 7th-century Arabs chose war over producing a counter-text. That itself is telling.
